subject: Hosting boundaries delineation for SIG evidence
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-sec.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify which hosting buckets were included in PT?

Hi Laura,

Quick question as we prepare the SIG/SOC2 evidence pack for Acme: can you confirm which of Redwood's hosting variants were in-scope for the most recent penetration test (March 2027)?

Specifically Acme needs: 1) Hosted (shared) API endpoints, 2) Dedicated (reserved) GPU pools, 3) Private (VPC) deployments managed by Redwood, and 4) On-prem packages we ship for air-gapped customers. Our intake form asks us to mark which of those were tested and whether any subcomponents (control plane, model-serving runtime, customer-managed network components) were excluded.

Can you provide a short categorization matrix and attach the relevant PT report stub or summary we can link in the SIG response? Also, if there are known outstanding remediation items that affect Hosted or Private customers, note those and expected completion dates.

Thanks — appreciate a concise table to include in our deliverable.

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Assessor, Acme Security

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-sec.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify which hosting buckets were included in PT?

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short PDF that maps our hosting categories to what was included in the March 2027 pen test and what was explicitly out-of-scope. Summary below (keeps to the concise table you requested):

- Hosted (shared API): INCLUDED — control plane + model-serving runtime + public ingress layers were tested. Note: third-party CDN edge nodes are out-of-scope.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): PARTIAL — the serving runtime and node OS were tested; dedicated customer configuration surfaces (customer-managed VPC peering setups) were not tested unless the customer opted into Redwood-managed networking (rare).
- Private (VPC, Redwood-managed): INCLUDED when Redwood manages the VPC and network stacks. Customer-managed VPCs (private deployments where customer controls networking) were OUT-OF-SCOPE.
- On-prem / air-gapped package: OUT-OF-SCOPE for the March test — those are verified via a separate supply-chain / install-audit process and we provide a separate checklist to customers.

A few clarifying notes:
- "Control plane" in our report = Redwood control plane services (auth, routing, telemetry). Those were tested for Hosted and Redwood-managed Private.
- "Model-serving runtime" = inference engine + memory/KV cache layers; included for Hosted and Dedicated nodes under Redwood management.
- Any integrations customers install into their private networks (e.g., internal observability forwarders, custom connectors) are not included unless explicitly onboarded for testing.

I attached: RI_InScope_Hosting_Categorization_20270330.pdf (the matrix you can paste into SIG responses) and a light remediation tracker export (RI_Remediation_Status_Q1_2027.xlsx) with high-level statuses.

Short timeline for outstanding items that might be relevant to Acme's risk review:
- Low: optional telemetry endpoint hardening for Hosted (ETA 2027-04-14).
- Medium: one beaconing issue in a 3rd-party telemetry dependency used in Dedicated images (mitigation patch rolled; full validation ETA 2027-04-21).
- High: no open high-severity findings affecting customer data plane exposure for any hosting variant.

Let me know if you need the actual full pen test report PDF (we can provide under NDA) or if Acme prefers a signed executive summary for SIG. Looping Rishi for any technical clarifications on the node-level remediation timelines.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0129

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-sec.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify which hosting buckets were included in PT?

Laura — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. Quick follow-ups so Acme can finalize the SIG:

1) For Dedicated pools: you note "partial" — can you confirm whether the KV cache persistence layer (used to store partial session artifacts) was in scope? Acme is specifically sensitive to persisted cache durability.
2) For Redwood-managed Private: are routing / load-balancer configs included in the test, or were those considered customer network components?
3) Can we get the signed executive summary (PDF) rather than the full pen test PDF — Acme procurement prefers the executive copy to attach to the SIG. NDA is in place but they still want the exec doc signed by the PT vendor.

If easier, a one-paragraph reply per question is perfect.

—Alex

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-sec.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify which hosting buckets were included in PT?

Alex — quick answers below (keeps it tight for the SIG record):

1) Dedicated KV cache persistence: INCLUDED for the tests carried out on Redwood-managed Dedicated nodes. The cache persistence layer (leveldb-based snapshotting) and the surrounding access controls were exercised in the March engagement. Persistent data stores that a customer manually mounts into Dedicated instances were out-of-scope.

2) Routing / LB configs for Redwood-managed Private: INCLUDED when the LB is provisioned and managed by Redwood (we test standard LB templates and our ACLs). If a customer brings their own LB inside their VPC and manages it, that component is out-of-scope.

3) Signed exec summary: yes — we can provide a vendor-signed executive summary PDF. Laura, Monica: we've attached the two files to this thread; I'll coordinate DocuSign for the exec summary. Monica, can you confirm the signature workflow and who at the vendor (PT firm) needs to sign?

Monica: FYI the remediation tracker contains the short status lines referenced earlier; nothing unresolved at severity "critical" that affects hosting boundaries. We'll deliver the exec summary by EOD tomorrow once DocuSign is completed.

-Rishi
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
